chunks: 2032 - In the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, it is reported that al-Sadiq عليه السلام said:

“In the last ten nights of the Month of Ramadan, say every night: I seek refuge in the majesty of Your noble Face lest the Month of Ramadan pass from me, or the dawn rise on this night of mine, while there remains upon me before You a claim or a sin for which You punish me, O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate.”

The supplication for the first night, which is the twenty-first night of the Month of Ramadan: “O You who cause the night to enter into the day, and cause the day to enter into the night; O You who bring forth the living from the dead and bring forth the dead from the living; O Provider of whomever You will without reckoning; O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Allah, O Most Compassionate, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, and to place my name on this night among the felicitous, my soul with the martyrs, my good in Illiyyin, my evil forgiven, and to grant me a certainty by which You make contact with my heart, and a faith by which doubt departs from me, and make me pleased with what You have apportioned for me, and give me”
“good in this world and good in the Hereafter”

“and protect me from the punishment of the Fire, and grant me therein gratitude to You, remembrance of You, desire toward You, turning back, repentance, and success for that to which You gave success to Muhammad and his family, Your blessings be upon them all.”

For the second night: “O You who strip the day out of the night, whereupon we are in darkness, and O You who cause the sun to run to its resting place by Your ordaining, O Mighty, O All-Knowing, and O Determiner of the moon”
“in phases until it returns like the old date stalk”

“O Light of every light, the ultimate end of every desire, and guardian of every blessing; O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Most Holy, O One, O Unique, O Singular, O Self-Sufficient; O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to place my name on this night among the felicitous.” Continue until you reach the end of the supplication of the first night. For the third night, which is Laylat al-Qadr: “O Lord of Laylat al-Qadr and the One who made it better”
“than a thousand months”

“and Lord of the night and the day, and Lord of the mountains and the seas, and the darknesses and the lights, and the earth and the sky; O Originator, O Fashioner, O Tenderly Merciful, O Great Bestower; O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Allah, O Self-Subsisting, O Allah, O Originator, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to place my name on this night among the felicitous.” To its end. And say in it: “O Allah, place in what You decree and determine of the fixed matter, and what You separate of the wise matter in Laylat al-Qadr, and in the decree that is neither repelled nor altered, that You write me among the pilgrims to Your Sacred House, whose hajj is accepted, whose striving is thanked, whose sins are forgiven, whose evil deeds are expiated from them; and place in what You decree and determine that You prolong my life, expand for me my provision, and free my neck from the Fire, O Most Merciful of the merciful.” And say in it: “O Manager of affairs, O Raiser of”
“those who are in the graves”

“O You who cause the seas to flow, O You who softened iron for Dawud, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and do for me such-and-such this night, this night, this hour, this hour.” Raise your hands to the sky and say it while you are prostrating, bowing, standing, and sitting, and repeat it, and say it on the last night of the Month of Ramadan.

For the fourth night: “O Splitter of the dawn, O Maker of the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning; O Mighty, O All-Knowing; O Possessor of favor, bounty, strength, power, grace, and beneficence; O Possessor of Majesty and Honor; O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Allah, O Singular, O Allah, O One, O Allah, O Manifest, O Hidden, O Ever-Living, there is no god but You. To You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.” Then complete it with the beginning of the supplication.

For the fifth night: “O Maker of the night as a covering, the day for livelihood, the earth as a cradle, and the mountains as pegs; O Allah, O Subduer, O Compeller, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.” Then complete it to its end.
For the sixth night: “O Maker of the night and the day as two signs, O You who effaced the sign of the night and made”
“the sign of the day illuminating”

“so that we may seek bounty from our Lord and good pleasure; O One who details everything in full detail; O Allah, O Glorious, O Allah, O Bestower, O Allah, O Generous, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and to place my name among the felicitous.” Then complete it to its end.

For the seventh night: “O Extender of the shade, and had You willed, You would have made it still, and You made the sun over it a guide, then You drew it toward You with an easy drawing; O Possessor of munificence, bounty, grandeur, and blessings; there is no god but You; O Most Holy, O Peace, O Giver of Security, O Overseer, O Mighty, O Compeller, O Supremely Great, O Creator, O Originator, O Fashioner; O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.” Then complete it to its end.

For the eighth night: “O Keeper of the night in the air, and Keeper of the light in the sky, and Preventer of the sky from falling upon the earth except by Your permission, and Holder of them both from passing away; O Tremendous, O All-Forgiving, O Everlasting, O Allah, O Everlasting, O Inheritor, O Raiser of”
“those who are in the graves”

“O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.” Then complete it.

For the ninth night: “O You who wrap the night over the day, and O You who wrap the day over the night; O All-Knowing, O Forbearing, O Wise; O Allah, O Lord of lords and Master of masters; there is no god but You; O One who is nearer to me”
“than the jugular vein”

“O Allah, O Allah, O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.” Then complete it with the opening of the supplication.

For the tenth night, which is the Night of Farewell: “All praise belongs to Allah, who has no partner. All praise belongs to Allah as is fitting for the nobility of His Face, the might of His Majesty, and as He is worthy of it. O Light, O Most Holy; O Light, O Most Holy; O All-Glorious, O ultimate limit of glorification; O Most Merciful, O Doer of mercy; O Allah, O All-Knowing; O Allah, O Gentle; O Allah, O Majestic; O Allah; to You belong the Most Beautiful Names, the Highest Similitudes, the Grandeur, and the Blessings. I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.” Then complete it with the opening of the supplication.

key_terms.السُّعَدَاءِ: the felicitous or blessed ones among whom the supplicant asks to be written
key_terms.الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى: the Most Beautiful Names of Allah invoked throughout the supplications
key_terms.حُجَّاجِ بَيْتِكَ الْحَرَامِ: the pilgrims of the Sacred House, among whom the supplicant asks to be recorded
key_terms.ذِكْرَكَ: Your dhikr, meaning remembrance of Allah sought as a provision in worship
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the sacred month in which these nightly supplications are recited
key_terms.عَذَابَ النَّارِ: the punishment of the Fire from which protection is sought
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: the exalted station associated here with the placement of one's good deeds
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree, a night of special divine determination and worship

ai.seo_question: What supplications are recited on each of the last ten nights of Ramadan according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a set of supplications for each of the last ten nights of the Month of Ramadan, with special emphasis on Laylat al-Qadr, forgiveness, acceptance of deeds, and nearness to Allah. The text invokes many divine attributes, asks for one's name to be written among the felicitous, and seeks pardon, rizq, certainty, iman, and salvation from the Fire.
